meaning.en: People follow so closely one after another that each sees the back of the next; describes a continuous stream of people or things.
meaning.zh: 前后的人互相都能看见对方的颈项和脊背，形容行人接连不断，非常拥挤。

examples.zh: 春运期间，火车站里旅客项背相望。
examples.en: During the Spring Festival rush, passengers at the station queue shoulder to back.

examples.zh: 景区开放首日，游客项背相望。
examples.en: On opening day the scenic area was thronged with a steady stream of visitors.

examples.zh: 通往山顶的小路上，登山者项背相望。
examples.en: Climbers followed one another closely all the way up the mountain path.

usage.en: Usually a predicate describing crowds or traffic. Neutral; fairly formal and written. Do not confuse with 望其项背 (to come close to someone's level), which is used in the negative: 难以望其项背.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，形容人流、车流络绎不绝。中性，偏书面。注意与“望其项背”（比得上，多用于否定）区别。

meaning.en: To hunch the shoulders and put on a forced smile in order to flatter someone powerful.
meaning.zh: 耸起肩膀，装出笑脸，形容谄媚奉承的丑态。

examples.zh: 他见了领导就胁肩谄笑，见了下属却趾高气扬。
examples.en: He fawns on his superiors but swaggers in front of his subordinates.

examples.zh: 真正有骨气的人不会为了升职而胁肩谄笑。
examples.en: A person of backbone will not grovel for a promotion.

examples.zh: 小说把那个胁肩谄笑的管家刻画得入木三分。
examples.en: The novel portrays the fawning steward vividly.

story.en: Mencius criticised those who 'hunch their shoulders and smile ingratiatingly, more weary than a farmer toiling in summer fields' (胁肩谄笑，病于夏畦).

usage.en: Strongly derogatory; used as a predicate or attributive, mostly in written style. Describes the look and manner of flattery.
usage.zh: 贬义，多作谓语、定语，书面语，侧重谄媚时的神态。

literal: rely on · power · play with · authority

meaning.en: To rely on one's position or influence to abuse authority for one's own ends.
meaning.zh: 倚仗权势，玩弄权力，为所欲为。

examples.zh: 那位官员挟势弄权，最终被依法查处。
examples.en: The official abused his power and was eventually prosecuted.

examples.zh: 家族企业里有人挟势弄权，大家敢怒不敢言。
examples.en: Someone in the family firm lords it over everyone and nobody dares to protest.

examples.zh: 历史上外戚挟势弄权的例子不胜枚举。
examples.en: History is full of cases of imperial in-laws abusing their power.

usage.en: Derogatory; predicate, written style. Note the first character is read xié (older reading jiā in some dictionaries).
usage.zh: 贬义，多作谓语，书面语。“挟”现读 xié。

meaning.en: Having a heart as firm as a boulder; unshakeable in one's determination or loyalty.
meaning.zh: 内心像大石头一样坚定，形容意志坚定，不可动摇。

examples.zh: 面对诱惑，他心如磐石，毫不动摇。
examples.en: Faced with temptation he stood firm as a rock.

examples.zh: 她对理想心如磐石，从未改变。
examples.en: Her devotion to her ideals has never wavered.

examples.zh: 他心如磐石，认定的路就一直走下去。
examples.en: His heart is set; once he picks a path he sticks to it.

usage.en: Predicate; praise. Describes resolve or fidelity, not stubbornness. Often paired with 志如钢铁.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，褒义，指意志或感情坚定，不是顽固。

meaning.en: To have lost all interest or enjoyment in something.
meaning.zh: 一点兴趣也没有了，形容对某事毫无兴致。

examples.zh: 讲座冗长无趣，听众渐渐兴味索然。
examples.en: The lecture was long and dull, and the audience gradually lost interest.

examples.zh: 他对这份工作早已兴味索然。
examples.en: He lost interest in this job long ago.

examples.zh: 连续加班一周，大家对聚会兴味索然。
examples.en: After a week of overtime, nobody felt like going to the party.

usage.en: Predicate; note 兴 is read xìng ('interest'), not xīng. The opposite is 兴致勃勃.
usage.zh: 多作谓语。“兴”读 xìng，不读 xīng。反义常用“兴致勃勃”。

meaning.en: To make trouble by spreading evil or nonsense; to cause mischief or disorder.
meaning.zh: 比喻坏人或坏思想捣乱作祟，制造混乱。

examples.zh: 有人在网上兴妖作怪，造谣生事。
examples.en: Some people are stirring up trouble online by spreading rumours.

examples.zh: 这个团伙在市场里兴妖作怪，欺压商贩。
examples.en: The gang makes trouble in the market and bullies the traders.

examples.zh: 别让几个害群之马在班里兴妖作怪。
examples.en: Don't let a few bad apples cause chaos in the class.

usage.en: Derogatory; predicate. Note 兴 is read xīng here ('to stir up').
usage.zh: 贬义，多作谓语。此处“兴”读 xīng，意为发动、兴起。

meaning.en: To act as a chivalrous hero, helping the weak and defending justice.
meaning.zh: 做侠义之事，扶助弱者，主持正义。

equivalents: act as a chivalrous champion of the weak

examples.zh: 他从小就喜欢武侠小说，梦想行侠仗义。
examples.en: He loved martial-arts novels as a child and dreamed of righting wrongs.

examples.zh: 这位老人一生行侠仗义，在街坊中口碑极好。
examples.en: The old man spent his life helping the weak and is well respected in the neighbourhood.

examples.zh: 电影里的主角行侠仗义，却不求回报。
examples.en: The film's hero fights for justice without asking for anything in return.

usage.en: Praise; predicate. Rooted in 武侠 culture, so slightly romantic; also used lightly of ordinary acts of courage.
usage.zh: 褒义，多作谓语，带有武侠文化色彩，也可轻松地指见义勇为。

meaning.en: Looking gaunt, withered and worn out, as from illness, grief or hardship.
meaning.zh: 身形瘦削，面容憔悴干瘪，形容人因病痛、忧愁或劳苦而消瘦憔悴。

examples.zh: 久病之后，他形容枯槁，几乎认不出来。
examples.en: After a long illness he was so gaunt as to be almost unrecognisable.

examples.zh: 流放多年，诗人形容枯槁。
examples.en: After years of exile the poet was haggard and thin.

examples.zh: 她为照顾病人心力交瘁，形容枯槁。
examples.en: Exhausted from nursing the patient, she became pale and worn.

story.en: Qu Yuan, wandering by the river, is described as 'haggard in face and gaunt in body' (颜色憔悴，形容枯槁).
story.zh: 《楚辞·渔父》：“颜色憔悴，形容枯槁。”

usage.en: Predicate or attributive; literary and gloomy. 槁 is read gǎo.
usage.zh: 多作谓语、定语，书面，色彩阴郁。“槁”读 gǎo。

literal: chest · no · city walls · government office

meaning.en: Being open and straightforward, with no hidden scheming; not secretive or calculating.
meaning.zh: 心里没有设防，待人坦率真诚，没有心机。

equivalents: wear one's heart on one's sleeve

examples.zh: 他胸无城府，有话直说。
examples.en: He is guileless and says what he thinks.

examples.zh: 孩子胸无城府，喜怒都写在脸上。
examples.en: Children are open; their joys and angers show on their faces.

examples.zh: 她胸无城府，容易被人利用。
examples.en: She is so open that people can easily take advantage of her.

usage.en: Usually praise, but can imply naivety. Opposite: 城府很深 (cunning, inscrutable).
usage.zh: 多为褒义，有时含天真之意。反义：城府很深。

natural: cultivate oneself and order the family

meaning.en: To cultivate one's own character and manage one's family well, the first steps of the Confucian path.
meaning.zh: 修养自身品德，管理好家庭，是儒家“修齐治平”的前两步。

equivalents: cultivate oneself and keep a good household

examples.zh: 古人讲究修身齐家，而后才谈治国。
examples.en: The ancients stressed self-cultivation and a well-run family before governing the state.

examples.zh: 家风建设要从修身齐家做起。
examples.en: Building a family tradition starts with self-cultivation and a well-ordered household.

examples.zh: 他把修身齐家当作人生的基本功。
examples.en: He treats self-cultivation and family harmony as life's basics.

story.en: The Great Learning lists the steps: 'cultivate the self, regulate the family, govern the state, bring peace to all under heaven' (身修而后家齐，家齐而后国治，国治而后天下平).
story.zh: 《礼记·大学》：“身修而后家齐，家齐而后国治，国治而后天下平。”

usage.en: Formal, often in essays on 家风 or Confucian ethics; usually the first half of 修身、齐家、治国、平天下.
usage.zh: 正式用语，常见于谈家风、儒家伦理的文章，常与“治国平天下”连用。

literal: repair · old · make use of · discarded

meaning.en: To mend old things and put discarded materials to use; a frugal, resourceful practice.
meaning.zh: 修理旧物，利用废料，提倡勤俭节约、物尽其用。

examples.zh: 工厂提倡修旧利废，每年节省成本上百万。
examples.en: The factory promotes repairing and reusing, saving millions a year.

examples.zh: 爷爷一辈子修旧利废，从不浪费。
examples.en: Grandpa spent his life mending and reusing, wasting nothing.

examples.zh: 社区开展修旧利废活动，鼓励居民环保。
examples.en: The community runs repair-and-reuse events to encourage green living.

usage.en: Praise; common in slogans and news about thrift or recycling.
usage.zh: 褒义，常见于节约、环保的标语和新闻。

meaning.en: To be ashamed of keeping company with someone; to refuse to associate with them out of disdain.
meaning.zh: 把和某人在一起看成羞耻的事，形容鄙视对方、不愿与之来往。

examples.zh: 正直的人羞与为伍，纷纷远离那个骗子。
examples.en: Honest people refused to keep company with the fraudster and stayed away.

examples.zh: 他对这种投机取巧之徒羞与为伍。
examples.en: He scorns to associate with such opportunists.

examples.zh: 在学术圈，抄袭者人人羞与为伍。
examples.en: In academia, nobody wants to be associated with plagiarists.

usage.en: Predicate with an object; shows disdain. Compare 耻与为伍 (same sense, rarer).
usage.zh: 多作谓语，带鄙视意味。

meaning.en: Rotten wood and filthy earth: a person too lazy or corrupt to be taught or improved.
meaning.zh: 腐烂的木头和脏土，比喻不可造就的人或不堪造就的事物。

examples.zh: 老师不愿把学生看作朽木粪土，仍耐心劝导。
examples.en: The teacher refused to treat the student as a hopeless case and kept patiently guiding him.

examples.zh: 这种制度已成朽木粪土，不改不行。
examples.en: The system is rotten through and cannot be saved without reform.

examples.zh: 别轻易说谁是朽木粪土，人是会变的。
examples.en: Don't be quick to call anyone hopeless; people change.

story.en: When Zai Yu slept in the daytime, Confucius said: 'Rotten wood cannot be carved; a wall of dung cannot be plastered' (朽木不可雕也，粪土之墙不可杇也).
story.zh: 《论语》：“朽木不可雕也，粪土之墙不可杇也。”

usage.en: Derogatory, formal; usually of a person who will not learn. Often quoted as 朽木不可雕 (rotten wood cannot be carved).
usage.zh: 贬义，书面，多指不肯上进、无法教育的人，常说“朽木不可雕”。

meaning.en: A whole universe inside a sleeve: great power or cleverness hidden in a small space or a modest appearance.
meaning.zh: 衣袖里藏着天地，比喻小处藏着大能耐，或指暗中另有安排、神通广大。

examples.zh: 这家小店袖里乾坤，菜单上有上百种地方小吃。
examples.en: This tiny shop is a world in itself, with over a hundred local snacks on the menu.

examples.zh: 魔术师的袖里乾坤，让观众惊叹不已。
examples.en: The magician's sleeve seemed to hold a whole world, amazing the audience.

examples.zh: 别看房子小，设计师做了个袖里乾坤的收纳系统。
examples.en: The flat is small, but the designer built a storage system that hides a surprising amount.

usage.en: Literary; often used lightly of clever use of small spaces, or of someone with hidden tricks. Compare 壶中天地.
usage.zh: 书面色彩，常轻松地形容小空间里藏着大学问，或指暗藏神通。

meaning.en: To completely change a dire situation; to reverse the course of events by great effort.
meaning.zh: 扭转天地，比喻彻底改变局面，具有重大的力量。

examples.zh: 新领导班子决心旋乾转坤，扭转企业的颓势。
examples.en: The new management is determined to turn the company's decline around.

examples.zh: 他有旋乾转坤的魄力。
examples.en: He has the nerve to turn the whole situation around.

examples.zh: 这场改革旋乾转坤，让小县城焕然一新。
examples.en: The reform transformed the small county completely.

usage.en: Praise; formal. Suggests a large-scale reversal, not a minor fix.
usage.zh: 褒义，书面，指大规模扭转局势。

literal: choose · the worthy · and · the able

meaning.en: To choose people of virtue and ability for public office.
meaning.zh: 选拔有德行、有才能的人来担任职务。

examples.zh: 古人理想的社会，是选贤与能、天下为公。
examples.en: The ancients' ideal society picked the worthy and able, and the world was shared by all.

examples.zh: 公司坚持选贤与能，不看关系看能力。
examples.en: The firm picks the able and virtuous, judging by ability, not connections.

examples.zh: 选贤与能是用人的基本原则。
examples.en: Choosing the worthy and able is the basic principle of recruitment.

story.en: The Liyun chapter describes the ideal 'Great Unity' (大同) society: 'the world is shared by all; the worthy and able are chosen; trust is spoken and harmony cultivated' (大道之行也，天下为公，选贤与能，讲信修睦).
story.zh: 《礼记·礼运》：“大道之行也，天下为公，选贤与能，讲信修睦。”

usage.en: Formal; 与 here is 'and' (a classical use, read yǔ), not 'give'. Often paired with 讲信修睦.
usage.zh: 正式用语，“与”意为“和”，读 yǔ。常与“讲信修睦”连用。

natural: sharpen one's head to a point

meaning.en: To go all out, by any means, to push into a place or get ahead, typically through scheming.
meaning.zh: 比喻千方百计、不择手段地钻营，想办法挤进某个圈子或谋取好处。

equivalents: jostle and scheme to get in
do whatever it takes to get ahead

examples.zh: 他削尖脑袋也要挤进那家大公司。
examples.en: He'd do anything to get into that big company.

examples.zh: 为了出名，有人削尖脑袋蹭热点。
examples.en: Some people will do anything to ride a trend and get famous.

examples.zh: 他削尖脑袋往上爬，同事们都看不惯。
examples.en: He's scheming to climb the ladder, and colleagues disapprove.

usage.en: Colloquial and usually critical; often 削尖脑袋往……钻/挤. The first character is read xuē in this phrase (xiāo is also heard).
usage.zh: 口语，多含贬义，常说“削尖脑袋往……钻”。“削”读 xuē（也可读 xiāo）。

meaning.en: Plain and simple words that carry deep meaning.
meaning.zh: 话语浅近，含义深远。

examples.zh: 这首小诗言近旨远，耐人寻味。
examples.en: This short poem uses simple words but carries deep meaning.

examples.zh: 老人的话言近旨远，值得年轻人深思。
examples.en: The old man's words are simple yet profound and worth pondering.

examples.zh: 好的寓言往往言近旨远。
examples.en: Good fables are often simple on the surface and deep beneath.

story.en: Mencius: 'Words that are plain yet whose meaning is far-reaching are good words' (言近而指远者，善言也).

usage.en: Praise for speech or writing. Not 言简意赅 (concise and to the point): 言近旨远 stresses depth beyond plain wording.
usage.zh: 褒义，用于话语或文章。与“言简意赅”不同，侧重含义深远。

meaning.en: The twittering of swallows and the song of orioles; describes lively spring scenery or a girl's sweet voice.
meaning.zh: 燕子低语，黄莺啼鸣，形容春天的美好景象，也形容女子悦耳的说话声。

examples.zh: 春天来了，园中燕语莺声，一派生机。
examples.en: Spring has come and the garden is alive with twittering birds.

examples.zh: 姑娘们燕语莺声，笑个不停。
examples.en: The girls chatted in sweet voices and laughed on and on.

examples.zh: 清晨的公园里燕语莺声，让人心情舒畅。
examples.en: Birdsong fills the park in the early morning, lifting the spirits.

usage.en: Literary and pleasant; scenery or voices. The order 莺声燕语 is also seen.
usage.zh: 书面，色彩优美，可形容景色或声音，也作“莺声燕语”。

meaning.en: To become famous and establish a reputation, often through a notable achievement.
meaning.zh: 传扬名声，树立威望，使自己名声远播。

examples.zh: 他想靠这部电影扬名立万。
examples.en: He hopes this film will make his name.

examples.zh: 年轻的拳手一心要在擂台上扬名立万。
examples.en: The young boxer is determined to make a name for himself in the ring.

examples.zh: 初来乍到的新人，都想找机会扬名立万。
examples.en: Every newcomer looks for a chance to make a name.

usage.en: Neutral to positive; common in martial-arts stories and modern sports or entertainment talk.
usage.zh: 中性偏褒，常见于武侠和体育、娱乐语境。

natural: a lamb in the tiger's jaws

meaning.en: A sheep entering a tiger's mouth: someone walking into certain danger or into the hands of a powerful enemy.
meaning.zh: 羊进入老虎嘴里，比喻处境极其危险，有去无回。

examples.zh: 让他一个人去谈判，无异于羊入虎口。
examples.en: Sending him alone to the negotiation is like sending a lamb into the tiger's mouth.

examples.zh: 夜里独自走那条僻静的路，简直是羊入虎口。
examples.en: Walking that deserted road alone at night is walking into danger.

examples.zh: 这个小公司被巨头收购，有如羊入虎口。
examples.en: The small firm's takeover by the giant was like a lamb in the tiger's jaws.

usage.en: Predicate or comparison (有如/无异于羊入虎口); often a warning. Compare 自投罗网.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，常用“无异于/有如羊入虎口”，多作警示。

meaning.en: A sheep wearing a tiger's skin: looking fierce or impressive on the outside but weak and timid within.
meaning.zh: 羊披着虎皮，比喻外表强大而内里怯弱，虚有其表。

examples.zh: 这家公司羊质虎皮，一遇风浪就垮了。
examples.en: The company is a paper tiger and collapsed at the first storm.

examples.zh: 别被他威风的样子骗了，不过是羊质虎皮。
examples.en: Don't be fooled by his swagger; he is a paper tiger.

examples.zh: 看似强大的对手，其实羊质虎皮。
examples.en: The seemingly strong opponent is in fact hollow.

story.en: Yang Xiong: 'A sheep in a tiger's skin delights at the sight of grass and trembles at the sight of a jackal' (羊质而虎皮，见草而悦，见豺而战，忘其皮之虎矣).
story.zh: 扬雄《法言》：“羊质而虎皮，见草而悦，见豺而战，忘其皮之虎矣。”

date.zh: 西汉末至新 · 前1世纪—1世纪
date.en: late Western Han to Xin, 1st c. BC–1st c. AD

usage.en: Derogatory; formal. Close to 外强中干 and 色厉内荏, but with the image of a disguise.
usage.zh: 贬义，书面，近于“外强中干”“色厉内荏”，但强调伪装。
